## Hypothesis

We need to validate whether the current engine (baseline configuration) achieves edge_capture > 771 and positive P&L when tested with walk-forward OOS on 2025-Q3 to 2026-Q2 and real-fills on the top 3 J days (4/29, 5/01, 5/04). The Stage-1 BS-synthetic baseline showed edge_capture=759.21 (<771 threshold), but OOS and real-fills behavior may differ due to regime shifts or simulation artifacts.

## Mechanism

No strategy changes are proposed. This candidate represents running the mandated validation tests on the current engine configuration:
- Walk-forward OOS: Train on 2025-Q1 to 2025-Q2, test on 2025-Q3 to 2026-Q2 (6 months OOS)
- Real-fills validation: Re-run top 3 J days (4/29, 5/01, 5/04) using cached real OPRA fills with realistic slippage model
- Metrics: edge_capture (per OP-16), aggregate Sharpe, wide P&L, quarterly consistency

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper ≈14% headline P&L (per risk-rules.md scaling)
2. **Sample bias:** OOS window = 6 months (2025-Q3 to 2026-Q2), 4 distinct regimes; real-fills sample = 3 anchor days only; overfit risk mitigated by walk-forward design
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (walk-forward test not yet executed)
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (validation on top 3 J days not yet executed)
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: potential -$300+ loss on 5/06 if engine fails to skip
   - Max drawdown: Stage-1 BS-sim showed $4,701.52; OOS may exceed
   - Blow-up scenario: consecutive losses on J winner days triggering daily kill switch
6. **Concentration:** Stage-1 BS-sim top5_pct=999.0 (single-day dominance); OOS may improve distribution
